1 big thing: Fresh inflation warning
 
Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED. Chart: Emily Peck/Axios

Prices for one of the world's least glamorous products — bare printed circuit boards — are skyrocketing to record levels, Axios' Emily Peck reports.

  • That's a blazing-loud warning for more inflation to come.

🟩 The big picture: Bare printed circuit boards are the green rectangles that house silicon chips.

  • They're in everything from smartphones and cars to medical and military equipment.

🤖 Data centers and AI labs are fueling huge price increases for computer chips — but also the simple boards that they get placed on.

  • The Producer Price Index for the boards rose 45% in July from the same time last year.
  • That reflects prices charged by domestic manufacturers. The U.S. produces only about 4% of the global supply, but the data still illustrates the pricing squeeze.

📈 Between the lines: The Iran war has pushed up prices for the boards' basic components: primarily resin and copper.

  • A major manufacturer of resin in Saudi Arabia was knocked offline in April after an Iranian attack.
  • That one plant makes 70% of the world's high-purity polyphenylene ether resin.

👀 What we're watching: Price hikes tied to higher circuit board costs will take a while to hit your wallet.

  • Jason Miller, a professor of supply chain management at Michigan State University's business school, tells Axios: "It takes at least six months, if not a year, for these price increases fairly far upstream in the supply chain to start to make their way to end users."

2. ✈️ Google buying Spirit data to feed AI
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Google is paying $10 million for Spirit Airlines' business data to feed into its AI models, Axios' Nathan Bomey reports.

  • The trove includes emails, calendar info, chats, documents, spreadsheets and more.

🤑 Google won a bankruptcy auction for the data from Spirit, which stopped flying earlier this year after failing to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

  • The data doesn't include any personally identifiable information, passenger profiles or frequent flyer info.

🤖 A Google statement says: "We acquired part of an enterprise dataset from Spirit Airlines, which can be helpful in improving our products and AI models."

What's next: A federal judge still needs to approve the deal.

4. 📱 1 tech thing: Meet the fixable smartphone
 

Image: Fairphone
 

Dutch tech company Fairphone is bringing its owner-repairable smartphone to the U.S., Wired reports.

  • The Android phone ships with a small screwdriver. Users can order replacement parts — screens, charging ports, etc. — directly from the company.

Fairphone CEO Raymond van Eck tells Wired: "If you look to the U.S. market, it's heavily duopolistic with very little real consumer choice."

  • "Americans are exhausted by planned obsolescence, closed-box ecosystems, and expensive yearly upgrades."
